basis: Congenital severe neutropenia is a blood-cell disorder and an innate immunodeficiency; infections do not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Inherited thrombocytopenia defines this phenotype; bleeding manifestations do not establish damage to additional organs, and clinically significant immunodeficiency is not defining.
Defined as an autoimmune neurologic syndrome associated with streptococcal infection; tics, chorea and developmental regression support nervous-system involvement.
Basal cell carcinoma variant arising in epidermis and extending into dermis; no common additional organ damage.
Benign Schwann-cell tumor arising from a peripheral nerve within the dermis; both cutaneous location and nerve origin define it.
Immune-mediated Crohn inflammation involving the anal region; anus belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inflammation of Tenon's capsule, an ocular supporting structure; inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune or infectious mechanism.
Benign smooth-muscle tumor arising in the fallopian tube; reproductive organ origin has no axis.
Immune-mediated type I interferonopathy umbrella; brain, skin and retinal damage vary by subtype, without established common involvement across the group.
Familial hemorrhagic diathesis is a coagulation disorder; bleeding alone does not establish another organ axis.
Thymic gland tumor maps to the supplied endocrine-gland category; thymic epithelial neoplasia alone does not establish lymphoma, autoimmunity or immunodeficiency.
Definition specifies isolated aniridia, with visual impairment in 8/8 and cataract in 6/8; inconsistent carcinoma and renal parents do not describe this disease.
Tumor arising in the cerebellum; vascular morphology and association with VHL do not establish additional organ involvement.
Definition and subtypes place this benign glandular/fibromyomatous tumor in female reproductive organs, which have no axis.
Scrotal integument is skin; scrotal tumors commonly arise in skin or its supporting soft tissue, including the listed melanoma subtype.
Malignancy of T/NK-lineage blood cells; lymphoma requires the immune mechanism axis. No extranodal site is common across this broad group.
Inherited surfactant phospholipid transport/metabolism defect directly causes alveolar accumulation and interstitial lung injury; manifestations are pulmonary.
Marrow disease defines FA; radial-ray defects, duodenal atresia and Chiari malformation each 1/1 reported. Abnormal GH response omitted at cap; renal frequency unknown.
Autoimmune disease of the neuromuscular junction; ocular and generalized weakness reflect impaired neuromuscular transmission, not separate eye or muscle injury.
Progressive inherited ataxia with retained reflexes; cardiomyopathy and skeletal deformities are less typical in this subtype, with no established frequency meeting 30%.
Degenerative cerebral white-matter disease with dementia, axonal loss and movement abnormalities; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than gastrointestinal damage.
Bronchiectasis establishes chronic structural airway disease; associated oligospermia affects reproduction, which has no axis.
Spinal osteoporosis and cataract/retinal disease define it; cardiac defects frequent (30-79%, several findings 2/2); sensorineural hearing loss 3/4.
Adipocytic sarcoma typically arising in deep soft connective tissue of the extremities; metastatic organs are not defining or uniformly common.
Occlusion of a retinal vein defines both the ocular site and venous vascular disease; associated systemic risk factors are separate conditions.
